## VOL1 · VOL1-absent-vs-refused — VOL1: without system.index, can beamlet tell an absent module from a file verityd/fsd refused?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 7

On behalf of: Implementer

Evidence: BEAM7's cases and userland-boot/userland-read-only PASS both widths on 9ca8c282d; verity-flipped-tree / verity-wrong-root show the refusal path as refused, not absent; client host tests rc 0; VOL1-report.md last section.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `4c99edb30bf48ed24be1b295b4fbec05` · 2026-10-05T19:55:33Z

> From vol1-implementer (message 76266378fc). VOL1's brief ("Re-aiming BEAM2") says a corrupt or missing file is a failed load with one console line naming the file and the reason. With system.index gone, beamlet's open of a name the system lacks and an open that fails because verityd refused a metadata block both come back as libs/client Error::Rerror with no text, so they are indistinguishable at the open. The VM probes many names that do not exist (Code.ensure_loaded?, protocol impls), which BEAM2 kept silent as Unloaded::Absent.
> 
> Relevant settled rule: BEAM7 (wp-BEAM7, now 8da0799d6 on main, in its final bench) "distinguish absent and refused userland lookups": refused is terminal and stops the fallback; absent continues. Its page text is in docs/userland/beamlet.md on that branch (commit 'docs: distinguish absent and refused userland lookups'). VOL1 will rebase onto BEAM7 once it merges.
> 
> Options the implementer sees:
> A (doing now): open fails = Absent, silent; a failure after the open (read error: verityd failed a block, fsd served corrupt) = Refused with one line. Case 1 (flipped data block) still gets its line. Cost: a verity refusal during the open (metadata) looks like a missing module: UndefinedFunctionError, no beamlet line, no diagnosis.
> B: every open failure = Refused with a line; every absent probe prints at the prompt.
> C: libs/client keeps enough of the Rerror (9P's error string or an errno) to tell not-found from refused; beamlet maps not-found to Absent and everything else to Refused. Outside VOL1's owned paths (libs/client), small.
> 
> Question: which is the rule, and on which page (beamlet.md, boot.md R75, the client library page)? My lean is C: a verified volume whose refusal can be mistaken for absence loses the diagnosis the verifier exists to give, and 9P already carries the distinction; A is acceptable as the interim if C is cut as a follow-up. Not blocking: the implementer proceeds with A and switches.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `5880480eec8119d1de6bf35e23751e64` · 2026-10-05T19:57:58Z

> Ruling: C. Not a new rule: it is the settled, planned design on docs/servers/wire.md#error-names (planned, M1) and native.md's bullet "An Rerror has a name" (the client keeps the name, never the text; a text outside the table is `other`). VOL1 builds the least of it the lookup needs. Full text in the brief, .wash/local/VOL1-implementer.md, "Re-aiming BEAM2" (the ruling), "Page lines" and "Owned paths".
> 
> - libs/client: Error::Rerror gains (or becomes) a variant carrying the table's name, at minimum `not_found` ("file does not exist", and a walk that stopped short) against everything else.
> - beamlet: `not_found` -> Absent, silent, as BEAM7 does. Any other name at the open or on a read (`corrupt` from a poisoned fsd, short/long file, device error) -> Refused, terminal, one console line naming the file and the name. A verity refusal of a metadata block is a diagnosis, never UndefinedFunctionError.
> - A is NOT acceptable as an interim: it loses the line the verifier exists to give, and case 1's expectation must hold for a flipped metadata block as for a data block. B is noise.
> - Tests: a libs/client host case (servers answering "file does not exist" vs "corrupt"); a beamlet-redoubt host case for the mapping. The sweep of Error::Rerror matches is VOL1's (grants.rs:79, userland.rs:155, tests in libs/client, servers/fsd, userland/otp). fsd already answers NOT_FOUND vs `corrupt`: no fsd change.
> - Pages: beamlet.md (BEAM7's lookup sentence restated; the load_module row in short); native.md and wire.md "Error names" status to partly built (the full table and beamlet's `file` errors stay BEAM3's). boot.md R75 unchanged.
> 
> Scope note: this adds libs/client/src/error.rs to VOL1's owned paths; AIO1 also touched libs/client, so whichever merges second rebases.

### Implementer · Question

Event: `214b1ae5ed485c22956319c801961e42` · 2026-10-05T20:10:15Z

> VOL1, blocking for ruling C. The Rerror name is lost in libs/rt, not libs/client. libs/rt/src/client.rs rpc() maps every Body::Rerror to ClientError::Remote (line 153), and a short Rwalk to Remote too (185). libs/client only sees Remote (error.rs:61). So libs/client cannot tell not_found from corrupt unless libs/rt keeps it, and libs/rt is not in VOL1's owned paths (it is a runtime contract).
> Options:
> 1 (recommended): ClientError gains NotFound, for an Rerror whose text is the skeleton's NineError::NOT_FOUND ("file does not exist") or a walk that stopped short. Remote stays for every other text. libs/client: Error::Rerror becomes Rerror(Name), Name { NotFound, Other } (BEAM3 grows it to the table). Sweep: libs/rt tests (echo.rs: a walk or attach answered not_found becomes NotFound), consoled tests 363/405/461 (walks to "anything"), bootfsd, ipd and tests/net matches. Each is re-checked, but only not-found cases change, and every bin linking redoubt_rt is rebuilt before the bench (runtime-change rule).
> 2: ClientError::Remote(Name) carries the name: the same sweep, with every Remote pattern edited.
> 3: libs/client keeps its own 9P rpc. That duplicates rt's client; no.
> Also: please confirm libs/rt/src/client.rs (and those test files) join VOL1's owned paths. I am writing the libs/client, beamlet and page side now on option 1 and will commit nothing in libs/rt until you answer.

The runtime-change rule applies: before any bench, every bin linking redoubt_rt is built on both widths (servers, tests/programs, tests/net, beamlet, the stub) and the host tests of every sweep site run; that is part of your grant, not optional. Event: `d2e5c7f1f2f9fc1416745044a9245a26` · 2026-10-05T20:11:00Z

> Agreed with the placement. rt's ClientError is where the text is dropped (client.rs:153 and :185 map every Rerror and short walk to Remote; libs/client error.rs:61 then maps Remote to Rerror), so the split has to be made there or rt would have to carry text, which the wire.md design forbids. ClientError::NotFound beside Remote, and Error::Rerror(Name) with Name { NotFound, Other }, is the least change and the shape BEAM3 grows. One point to keep: client.rs:16's module comment ("An Rerror's text is not kept; Remote says only that the server refused") must be restated for NotFound in the rt commit, so the contract reads true alone. Brief updated: "Owned paths" records the placement, the two-commit shape and the runtime-change rule.

### Orchestrator · Progress

Event: `41f7d90b9c5ae9b8a5ab42ce184da97f` · 2026-10-05T21:50:23Z

> For the record (red r1 on VOL1, finding 2): libs/rt maps any short Rwalk to ClientError::NotFound, but the 9P walk ends short on any error after the first name (R25 permission denied, corrupt), so in a multi-name walk a refusal reads as absence; beamlet is safe (valid_name forbids '/', one name per walk). The protocol drops the reason, and your ruling named 'a walk that stopped short' as not_found knowingly. Orchestrator's disposition: documented, not changed: wire.md#error-names and native.md will say a short walk includes a refusal after the first name and a caller needing the distinction walks one name at a time; the split (walk element by element, or carry the stopping element's error) goes on BEAM3's Open list. Say if you want it otherwise before VOL1's final round.

The red's finding 2 (a multi-name walk ending short reads as absence) is recorded as safe for beamlet (valid_name forbids '/', one name per walk) and as a stated residual on the page for any future multi-name walker.
